assets.edits: Green background keyed to alpha and despilled. Then four edits with sharp. The left arm was replaced by the top arm mirrored across the diagonal, outside the rose window, so the two arms match exactly. The briar stems outside the rose window were shifted from dull garnet to blood red; the pale thorns and the window were left as painted. The painting was moved 1.5 percent up and left so the top arm lies on the iron line of the frame's top rail. The left arm was then moved a further 2.8 percent outward and 2.2 percent up, behind the window, because the frame paints the iron line of its side rails nearer their outer edge (about 7px of 26) than that of its top and bottom rails (about 12px of 26).
assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. One production fantasy game interface corner fitting, square image, front-facing orthographic, lit flat from the front, on a perfectly flat pure green #00FF00 background with no shading and no cast shadows (it will be keyed out to transparency). A TOP LEFT corner fitting. At the corner sits ONE round Gothic rose window exactly like the one in the first attached image: a circular ring of antique rose-tinted silver tracery holding eight petal-shaped panes of deep garnet-red stained glass around a small silver hub. It is a free-standing round medallion: there is NO square stone block, NO plate and NO studs around it, only the round silver ring with a thin blackened iron rim, and flat green background all around the circle. From the medallion two arms run along the TOP edge and the LEFT edge only. Each arm is NOT a bar of stone or metal: it is a ribbon made only of thorned briar stems, two or three thin dark stems, almost black with a dull garnet tint, plaited loosely together like a braid, with sharp pale thorns and no leaves, and flat green background showing through the gaps of the braid and on both sides of it. There are no quatrefoils, no symbols, no studs and no stone on the arms. One or two small dark-red rosebuds, seen from straight above so they are round, sit in the braid of each arm. The braid is about 7 percent of the image wide where it leaves the medallion, stays that width for most of its length, then thins steadily over its last third to a single fine stem ending in a point within the canvas, leaving a small green margin, so it can lie over a continuous rail and fade into it. A short loop of briar curls around the outside of the medallion ring. The stems are bare and do not hang or droop, so the design reads correctly upside down or mirrored; the two arms mirror each other across the diagonal from the top-left corner. The rose window is a circle about 27 percent of the image wide, tucked into the top-left corner with a small green margin between it and the image edges. The top arm leaves the right side of the circle with its centre line 10.5 percent from the top edge; the left arm leaves the bottom of the circle with its centre line 10.5 percent from the left edge. The entire lower-right 70 percent square must be completely flat green and EMPTY. Rich hand-painted realistic strategy-game UI art, sculpted volume, austere medieval cathedral craft, dusty silver highlights, no gold. Do not use green, teal or lime anywhere in the fitting: briars are near-black and dull garnet, never green. No leaves, no scenery, no text, no skulls, no crosses, no creatures, no frame around the image, no shadow on the background.
